newsitem.title: USA: Delta in final stage of aircraft talks.
newsitem.headline: Delta in final stage of aircraft talks.

text.p: Delta Air Lines Inc. said Tuesday it was in final discussions with Boeing Co. and European consortium Airbus Industrie for a major aircraft order, but refused to discuss the possibility of an exclusive deal with Boeing.
The final deal could go beyond an initially stated goal of two dozen wide-bodied jets, needed to help retire 49 ageing Lockheed L-1011 airliners from Delta's domestic routes.
"As part of the retirement process, we're looking for approximately two dozen wide-body aircraft. That's what is a priority," Delta spokesman Bill Berry said.

"The discussions have progressed to the point where it could be a package, in other words airplanes in addition to just the replacement of the L-1011s. But we've been no more definitive than that," he added.
Delta Chairman Ron Allen and other senior executives recently have visited Boeing and Airbus facilities. But a final agreement could still be a ways off.

"We are now in very sensitive final discussions with the manufacturers ... we would hope to have a decision in a matter of weeks. But I can't tell you if it's two weeks or six weeks or eight weeks," Berry said.

The Delta spokesman declined to discuss the potential size of any future deal, and specifically avoided comment on a Wall Street Journal report saying the airline could buy 100 planes worth $6 billion in an exclusive deal with Boeing similar to Boeing's $6.5 billion deal with American Airlines.
Berry also declined to say whether a new major order would go to a single manufacturer despite industry trends toward streamlined fleets. Delta Air Lines has never had an exclusive supplier.
Part of Delta's appetite for new planes stems from its launch of the low-cost Delta Express service with 25 Boeing 737-200 aircraft.
Despite the express operation's success, its ability to expand has been limited by demand for the remaining Delta 737s from its booming full-line service.
Berry also said Delta could look to replace the older Boeing 727s in its fleet. "But we haven't identified anything as far as numbers of airplanes or what we would be replacing," he added.
